newsitem.title: USA: TV executives unveil ratings program.
newsitem.headline: TV executives unveil ratings program.

text.p: Television industry executives on Thursday unveiled their controversial system to rate programmes, ushering in a new era for TV meant to enable parents to better control their children's viewing habits.

Broadcast and cable-TV networks will begin displaying the ratings before their shows in January. The age-based system is similar to the 28-year-old ratings used by the motion-picture industry and will apply to all shows, except news and sports programmes.

But even before its formal unveiling by network executives in a statement here the new system had drawn flak from lawmakers, parental groups, children's advocates, educators and others. They want the ratings content-based and to specify the level of sex, violence and strong language.
The ratings cover six categories: TV-G for suitable for all ages; TV-PG for parental guidance suggested; TV-14 for parents of children under 14 strongly cautioned; and TV-M for mature audiences only.
Two categories apply to children's shows: TV-Y for all children; and TV-Y7 for kids seven and older.
Networks and distributors will rate their own shows, unlike the movie-industry system in which an independent panel rates the films.
